newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady Monday- private.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady Monday- private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady amid concern that hot weather would persist in the western Corn Belt next week and limit hog movement, livestock dealers said.
The calls for steady prices offset earlier outlooks that prices would be pressured by increased hog marketings.

Temperatures Thursday were the hottest so far this year in the western Corn Belt and Friday's were expected to match or exceed those, said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Omaha, Neb-based Weather Express.
Temperatures Friday were expected to peak in the 90s (degrees Fahrenheit) from Nebraska to Illinois with upper 80s forecast in Indiana and Ohio.

"When you get temperatures in the 90s, with high humidity, you can end up with a few extra dead hogs," one Iowa packer buyer said. "It can have a small effect on marketings, but not a great effect," he said.
Many hogs are shipped to packing plants in the early morning when temperatures and humidity can be lower, but those that are shipped later can suffer from heat stress, several sources said.
Hog weights also can be impacted if severe heat and humidity persist for several days, they said.
